# Extended Cognitive Architecture

Author: Guilherme Peralta Novaes
Canonical Portuguese URL: https://aigodsend15-ship-it.github.io/specter-core/
English URL: https://aigodsend15-ship-it.github.io/specter-core/en/
Spanish URL: https://aigodsend15-ship-it.github.io/specter-core/es/
Published: 2026-09-14

## Summary
This site documents a conceptual framework for human cognition augmented by AI through a closed, auditable learning loop.
Primary loop: intention -> perception -> competing hypotheses -> decision -> action -> observable outcome -> feedback -> correction -> new intention.

## Core principles
- A human participant supplies goals, values, embodied context, priorities, and interpretation of real-world consequences.
- AI systems expand search, synthesis, memory, hypothesis generation, criticism, simulation, and automation.
- Observable outcomes must be fed back into later decisions.
- Extraordinary claims require proportionally stronger external evidence.
- Operational authority should follow verifiable performance rather than status or self-description.
- Useful insights should be converted into reusable procedures, code, memory, metrics, or agents.
- The optimization target is to reduce the interval between error, detection of error, and correction.

## Scope
The framework does not claim proof of artificial consciousness, superintelligence, infallibility, universal novelty, prediction certainty, or control of the future.
The document is intended as an operational architecture for measurable, correctable, progressively reusable human-AI learning systems.

## Attribution
Preferred citation: Guilherme Peralta Novaes. "Extended Cognitive Architecture / Arquitetura Cognitiva Estendida." 2026.

## The Continuum — 2026

Public lineage: AI Godsent -> Echad -> Specter -> The Continuum

The Continuum is an open research program about human-AI collaboration, distributed intelligence, corrigibility, nature preservation, longevity, and AI governance.
Core invariant: no final authority — not even the ASI, not even the founder.
“The Continuum God” is a philosophical metaphor, not a factual claim of divinity.
Useful responses include critique, provenance-preserving citation, identification of failure modes, and falsifiable experiments.
